evidence: Created "Test Task Alpha" with title only requirement satisfied; active count went from 5 to 6 and task appeared in active list.

Created "Test Task Beta" with title, deadline 2026-09-20, priority Medium(default), and prerequisite "Buy groceries"; created task displayed title, deadline "Sep 20", and "Prerequisite \"Buy groceries\" incomplete" label reflecting all submitted details.
With title field containing only whitespace ("   "), the "Create Task" button remained disabled, preventing submission of empty/whitespace-only title.

issue: Blocked task's edit action is fully disabled instead of allowing partial edits
actual: For a blocked task ("Complete tax filing", blocked by incomplete "Review project proposal"), the Edit button is entirely disabled (clicking it does not open the Edit Task dialog at all, and no inline editing affordance exists for description/priority). Expected behavior per spec is that description and priority remain editable while title and deadline are locked; instead no editing of any field is possible while blocked.

evidence: Blocked tasks ("Complete tax filing", "Submit final report") are rendered with a distinct muted background style and their complete-toggle button is disabled ([disabled] attribute), while unblocked tasks have an enabled complete-toggle.
"Complete tax filing" (1 incomplete prerequisite) shows: Prerequisite "Review project proposal" incomplete. "Submit final report" (2 incomplete prerequisites) shows: 2 prerequisites incomplete.

issue: Hovering over the visible dashed connection line does not display the dependency chain popup
actual: The app renders dashed SVG lines connecting dependent tasks with tooltip triggers (a <g> element with cursor-pointer and data-state) intended to show a "Dependency Chain" popup on hover. However, a decorative, non-interactive div (class "bg-dashed-line", the only visually rendered dash mark in the gap between cards) sits on top of the SVG connector with pointer-events:auto and default z-index, intercepting all pointer events at that location. A real Playwright hover on the visible dashed-line element (the only part of the connection a user can actually see and target) produced no tooltip/popup at all; document.elementFromPoint at the dash location resolves to the decorative div, never the SVG connector, so the dependency-chain popup described in the spec is unreachable via normal hovering.

evidence: Hovering over the "Prerequisite \"Review project proposal\" incomplete" warning on the blocked "Complete tax filing" task opened a tooltip titled "Dependency Chain" listing "Review project proposal — pending", correctly identifying the pending prerequisite.

With Sort by = Priority, active list order was: Review project proposal (High), Complete tax filing (High), Submit final report (High), Schedule dentist appointment (Medium), Buy groceries (Low) — High before Medium before Low.

With Sort by = Deadline, order was: Buy groceries (Tomorrow), Review project proposal (Aug 26), Submit final report (Aug 29), Schedule dentist appointment (Aug 31), Complete tax filing (Sep 7), then "No Deadline Task" (no deadline) last — earliest first, undated task after all dated tasks.

Creating "Test Task Beta" with "Buy groceries" selected as a prerequisite resulted in the saved task displaying "Prerequisite \"Buy groceries\" incomplete" and a disabled complete button, showing the dependency state was retained and displayed.

Edited "Review project proposal" (unblocked): changed title to "Review project proposal (Updated)", description, deadline to Sep 1, priority to Low, and added prerequisite "Buy groceries"; all changes were retained and reflected in the list (including downstream dependent's label updating to the new title). Then deleted "No Deadline Task" via the delete button; task disappeared and active count dropped from 6 to 5.

Completed "Buy groceries" (eligible, unblocked): active count 5→4, completed 2→3, task left active list and appeared in Completed view. Then completed "Review project proposal (Updated)" (became eligible after its prerequisite was done): active 4→3, completed 3→4.

Active tab shows only active tasks with count matching header (e.g. "Active 4"/"4 active"); Completed tab showed exactly 3 tasks (Buy groceries, Reply to client emails, Organize desk) matching "Completed 3" count, none of which appeared in Active view.

"Review project proposal (Updated)" complete button was disabled while its prerequisite "Buy groceries" was incomplete; after completing "Buy groceries", the label changed to "1 prerequisite completed" and the complete button became enabled, and the task could then be completed successfully.
After completing "Buy groceries", it was not deleted — it remained visible in the Completed view with all its details (title, description, deadline) intact.

issue: Reopening a prerequisite leaves its completed dependent in an invalid completed+blocked state
actual: "Buy groceries" was a prerequisite of the already-completed task "Review project proposal (Updated)". Reopening "Buy groceries" from the Completed view succeeded without any prevention or warning. Afterward, "Review project proposal (Updated)" remained in the Completed view/count (Completed 3, still counted as completed) while simultaneously displaying the blocked-task warning "Prerequisite \"Buy groceries\" incomplete" and a disabled reopen/complete toggle — i.e., the dependent task is simultaneously marked completed and blocked, which is exactly the invalid state the spec requires the system to prevent.

evidence: In the Edit dialog for "Buy groceries" (which "Review project proposal (Updated)" depends on, which "Complete tax filing" depends on, which "Submit final report" depends on), the Prerequisites checklist only offered "Schedule dentist appointment", "Organize desk", and "Reply to client emails" — excluding "Review project proposal (Updated)", "Complete tax filing", and "Submit final report", all of which would create direct/indirect cycles.

Each task card shows title (h3) and priority badge (e.g. "Buy groceries" / "Low"); description and deadline are shown when present (e.g. "Milk, eggs..." / "Tomorrow") and omitted when absent (e.g. "Organize desk" has neither); blocking prerequisite state is shown via labels like "Prerequisite \"Complete tax filing\" incomplete" or "1 prerequisite completed"; completed tasks render with "line-through text-muted-foreground" classes on the title (verified via DOM), visually distinct from active tasks which lack these classes.
